reference.title: Hazard: Flying Chips During Machining
reference.shortdesc: Hot, sharp metal chips ejected at high velocity during cutting operations pose eye and skin injury risks.

messagepanel.consequence: Severe eye injury or skin laceration
messagepanel.howtoavoid: Always wear safety glasses with side shields when the machine door is open or during chip clearing. Keep the machine door closed during all cutting operations.

section.title: Hazard Description
section.p: During milling, drilling, and tapping operations on the MC-5000 VMC, cutting tools generate metal chips that are ejected at velocities up to 30 m/s. These chips are:

ul.li: Sharp — can penetrate skin and cause lacerations
Hot — can reach 200–400°C immediately after cutting
Projectile — can bounce off shields and reach the operator

section.p: The primary risk period is during chip clearing and part inspection when the door may be briefly opened.

strow.stentry: Interlock stops spindle if door opens
Manual chip clearing with door open

ul.li: Machine interlock system (Zone 1 door) — automatically stops spindle if door is opened
PPE: ANSI Z87.1 rated safety glasses with side shields
PPE: Cut-resistant gloves during chip handling
Machine chip guard at the door bottom (height: 150 mm)
ISO 12100:2010 — Risk assessment and risk reduction
ISO 13849-1 — Safety-related parts of control systems
ANSI Z87.1 — Occupational and educational eye protection
